jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Tuvalu has no national AI law, strategy or official AI guidance. Its 2021 National ICT Policy lists AI among several emerging technologies the government wants frameworks for, but has no AI pillar or AI-specific measures. AI otherwise appears only in donor-supported projects such as AI-based weather forecasting and a national digital twin. The digital agenda runs through the National ICT Policy and the Digital Nation initiative.
lead_institutions: Department of Information and Communications Technology
narrative.review_notes: The national legislation portal, Parliament's website and the Ministry of Finance and Economic Development (including its procurement unit) were searched on 18 October 2026 and no AI-specific law, bill or guidance was found; the ICT department's and the main government portal's websites could still not be accessed. The 2021 National ICT Policy was reviewed and is listed under Leads because it mentions AI only in passing, and pending cybercrime and electronic transactions bills also remain under Leads.

leads.title: National ICT Policy 2021 (Tuvalu)
leads.issuing_authority: Government of Tuvalu (foreword by the Minister of Justice, Communication and Foreign Affairs)
leads.note: 2026-10-18: official text read on the Ministry of Finance and Economic Development site (https://finance.gov.tv/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/National-ICT-Policy-2021.pdf). The document is the 2021 National ICT Policy (replacing the 2014 Draft National ICT Policy), not a 2023 policy as earlier secondary reports suggested; no approval or publication date is printed. It sets seven strategic focus areas (infrastructure and access, government services, cyber security and cyber safety, universal access, digital transformation, ICT human capacity, and others) with no AI pillar. AI is mentioned only in passing: one objective is to facilitate frameworks for emerging technologies 'like Big Data, IoT, Blockchain, 5G, and AI', and a background section describes machine learning. Held as a lead under the scope test (passing mention); reconsider for 'strategy' only if the lead reviewer judges the emerging-technology objective sufficient.

leads.title: Cybercrime Bill (Tuvalu, pending)
leads.issuing_authority: Government of Tuvalu / Parliament of Tuvalu
leads.note: Reported by secondary sources as drafted and pending (no dedicated cybercrime statute enacted); no official text located. Check for any AI/deepfake provisions once published on tuvalu-legislation.tv. 2026-10-18: Tuvalu legislation portal now reachable; full-text search for 'cybercrime' returned no results, the Bills section lists no bills for 2020-2026, and no cybercrime act is listed among 2020-2025 acts. Still unpublished.

leads.title: Electronic Transactions Bill (Tuvalu)
leads.note: Reported in 2023 as being prepared after a 2020 gap analysis covering electronic transactions, data protection, consumer protection and cybercrime; status unknown; no official text located. Unverified secondary reports also mention a 'Data Protection and Privacy Act 2020' that could not be confirmed on any official source. 2026-10-18: Tuvalu legislation portal now reachable; no Electronic Transactions Act or bill and no data protection act is listed among 2020-2025 acts (the 2020 acts list has no 'Data Protection and Privacy Act'), and the Bills section lists no bills for 2020-2026. Still unverified.

leads.title: National Security Policy (Tuvalu, in development)
leads.note: Reported in development after Cabinet endorsement in September 2025, covering cyber security among other areas; no official text located and no indication of AI content. 2026-10-18: no official text found on the reachable official sites (legislation portal, Parliament, Ministry of Finance).
